label: Catalog anchors re-verified; token tier is the check

The playbook census denominator was conflated: the 2,682 .md files iteration 8 reported are the path-substring population (any path containing manual-testing-playbook), not the 57 exact manual-testing-playbook trees; the exact-tree population is 1,465 files carrying 1,375 SCENARIO CONTRACT files (93.9%), while the broad pair 2,682/1,382 is self-consistent at 51.5%. The validator discovers packages as <skillsRoot>/<filter>/manual-testing-playbook, so the spec corpus scope must be the exact-tree rule; the 1,217 broad-only files (925 under cli-external-orchestration benchmarks) are report corpora, not playbook packages.

The markdown-link half restated: the exact-tree corpus carries 4,986 link instances / 1,987 distinct relative targets, zero .skilled/.opencode-prefixed targets (iteration 8's 1,271 prefixed links do not reproduce), exactly 1 unresolved target — a missing-link fixture whose target is named definitely-missing-link-target-for-guard-verification.md inside the link-integrity guard scenario — plus 9 directory targets and 7 code-block artifacts. The link gate's basis is per-file relative resolution, and the extractor needs a code-fence/instruction exclusion.

Inline-citation resolution ladder measured over 12,959 instances / 3,952 distinct tokens in the exact tree: root-only resolves 1,906 instances (14.7%); adding skill-root, scripts, runtime, skill-subtree basename and global basename resolves 11,281 (87.0%). Residual 1,678 instances / 773 distinct decomposes into placeholder/glob 449, scratch /tmp and $VAR 370, bare basenames absent anywhere 565, other 233, runtime/generated 46, migrated-named 12, provenance 3. The dominant stage is skill-subtree basename (5,840 instances), so the spec's base-resolution order and expected-unresolved families are what make an existence check viable, not the anchor format.

Catalog replay with a corrected extractor: 36 anchors across 6 of 611 catalog files; 34 resolve (root 26, skill/runtime 5, skill 3) and the 2 unresolved are the annotated memory-server removals; the bounds check fires 0/36. Token-at-line fires 9/36: the three stale system-skill-advisor anchors confirmed live (schemas/advisor-tool-schemas.ts compiledRoute 221 -> 268; advisor-status.ts 89-94 -> 344/345; skill-advisor-cli.ts 1420-1440 -> 1500/1501), the four loose anchors from iteration 7, one newly adjudicated loose anchor (tools/index.ts 37-43; advisor_rebuild actually at 59), and the canonical true positive pinned: the row at code-standards-alignment.md:76 cites runtime/handlers/save/spec-folder-mutex.ts:10, which is an import line; SPEC_FOLDER_LOCKS is defined at line 22. The check's entire discriminating power is the judgment-bound token tier.

The prose file-line-N form is not a singleton: with a complete extension set it numbers 13 instances across 12 files (seven ../../SKILL.md line N in cli-external-orchestration trees, .hermes/SYNC.md line 1, mcp-code-mode SKILL.md 232-233, sk-code SKILL.md 78-90, stack-detection.md 50-62, rollback-lifecycle.md 1-72, debug.md 60-89, and create.sh line 1084); iteration 8's exactly-1 count was an extractor artifact of an extension set missing md. The class needs its own extractor branch and fixtures; the literal-naming create.sh citation remains the only code-file instance.

Extractor defects are the recurring failure mode and must ship as regression fixtures: js-before-json truncation (iteration 7), the backtick-separated line form (iteration 8), leading-dot loss plus a prefix off-by-one in the skill-base resolver (iteration 9), and a missing md in the extension alternation (iteration 9). Each silently skewed a headline number before correction; the spec must define candidate token precisely and pin corpus fixtures as extractor tests.
